items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: Well, who did he play with after he played with Amos White? ... Amos left his and went up the north.

ctx.x: Well, who did he play with after he played with Amos White?

So who did you play with after you played with Amos White? Amos White? Amos White. Uh-huh. Yeah. Amos left his and went up the north. And we, we hold up our bag until things got dead. Then we start to go from one place to another, you know. Then I last went to Alexander, you know. Stayed over there about almost four years, you know. Meet a bunch of fellas from here sometime, be over there with us. Like Dr. Noah. Then when I come back, I said, that's back where I tell you. See, I tell you, he picked me up. And…
Ask him who he was playing with when depression came.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: Did you know Amos White? You know Amos White?

ctx.x: I'm asking did they have a new Liberty Bell?

So did you have a new Liberty Bell? A new Liberty Bell? New? New? Did they have a new Liberty Bell band? A new Liberty Bell band? No, not after we broke up. But our band got popular. And all of them all the world, they know them. They know them. They're like Willie Hump and all of them. Lewis Armstrong. All them fellas like that. Did you know Amos White? You know Amos White?
I didn't know him. You never know that? He's in California.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: And Amos White, Fred Kyle Coates. You got his name, I said, you know. He had a little bit of a tripper. He was a little fella like me. And he wanted to be a big shot today. He said, he had his legs straightened. And he left his, got the band, went to California.

ctx.x: I'll say. I'll say. I'll say.

I'll say. I'll say. I'll say. My band was still up then. And that's where I told them we had Maurice and, uh, Rika Ellis. I'll say. Rika Ellis. Rika Ellis. I don't know why Rika left us, but we got, uh, uh, Maurice here. He just come from World of War, you know. First World of War, you know. And then he got in and I'm going to start the bossing, you know. And we said, yeah, we're all young boys, you know, get a band over in the community, try to run all bands along as we've been up. And that's why we kept on and…
I used to lead it for him to catch it. He said, when he catch it, he had a good laugh.
